title: Scripture and Evangelism
definition: Scripture and evangelism belong together because the Gospel message is revealed in the Word and faith comes by hearing the word of Christ.
summary: Evangelism must proclaim the biblical truth about God, sin, Christ, repentance, faith, forgiveness, and eternal life.
christFocus: Christ is the message of evangelism, and Scripture bears witness to His death and resurrection for sinners.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Scripture and Evangelism teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to scripture and evangelism by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
